subject: Business
title: The Pirate Metrics Framework
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Pirate Metrics Framework.

hook.text: Dave McClure reduced startup growth to five letters: AARRR. It sounds like a pirate, and it stuck.

buildup.text: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Revenue, Referral — each measures a different stage.

discovery.text: Most startups obsess over acquisition and ignore activation — getting users to the first 'aha' moment.

twist.text: Fixing retention often matters more than acquiring new users. A leaky bucket never fills.

climax.text: Twitter found that users who followed 30 people were far more likely to stay. That became their focus.

punchline.text: Measure each stage. Then fix the weakest link.

quiz.question: What does AARRR stand for in Pirate Metrics?

details.summary: Dave McClure's Pirate Metrics framework organizes startup growth into five stages: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Revenue, and Referral, abbreviated as AARRR. Each stage represents a step in the customer journey and provides specific metrics that identify where growth is blocked.

takeaways: AARRR covers acquisition, activation, retention, revenue, and referral stages
Each stage has specific metrics that reveal where the growth funnel breaks down
Focus on optimizing the weakest stage rather than spreading effort across all five

faq.question: What does each letter in AARRR measure?
faq.answer: Acquisition measures how users find you. Activation measures whether first-time users have a good initial experience. Retention measures whether they come back. Revenue measures whether they pay. Referral measures whether they tell others. Each stage has specific conversion metrics.

faq.question: Which AARRR metric should startups focus on first?
faq.answer: Retention first. If users are not coming back, pouring more users into the top of the funnel is waste. Retention validates product-market fit. Once retention is healthy, optimize activation so that new users experience the product's value. Then scale acquisition to fill a proven funnel.
